body:
Stacked on #7280 → #7277.

## Summary
- The direct-mic channel of a stereo capture has always been treated as the local user alone (`plan_channel` skipped `(2,2,0)`, the renderer hard-wires `DirectMic` to "You"). That only holds for calls; an in-person meeting recorded from one laptop rendered everyone as "You".
- New `in_person_capture`: a capture is in person when the session expected ≥2 participants (`num_speakers`/`min_speakers`) yet the system-audio channel carried ≤3 s of speech — nobody was on the call, so everyone was in the room. Headphone state is deliberately not a gate: it keeps the far end out of the mic, not the people beside it. Unknown participant counts stay closed, since a solo memo and a two-person meeting sound the same to the recorder.
- When in person, ch0 takes the full participant count: `apply_local_diarization` separates it with `SpeakerBounds::exact(total)`, and `consolidate_hosted_speakers` caps a hosted provider's mic labels to it. `channel_audio`/`plan_channel`/`could_plan_channel` gain an `in_person` flag; the remote channel keeps its call-shaped budget.
- Surfacing: only when ≥2 speakers actually come out of ch0 are its words moved to channel 2 (`MixedCapture`). The renderer then shows "Speaker N" (capped by participant count), speaker naming and voiceprint matching work in the `mixed_capture` domain, and the isolated-mic self-exemplar path no longer sees those words. A mic that still sounds like one voice is left exactly as before. Hosted transcripts whose provider already split the mic correctly are relabeled without decoding audio.
- `diarize_channels` takes a `DiarizeJob` struct (clippy `too_many_arguments`).

## Not in this PR
- Live transcripts still show "You" during an in-person meeting; the separation lands with the post-meeting refine.
- The desktop only triggers refine for >1 remote participants, so an in-person 1:1 is not yet separated. That gate could use "remote channel was silent" as an additional trigger.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p listener2-core` (93). New real-audio tests on an in-person fixture (both `english_1` speakers on the mic, silence on system audio): local diarization finds two people and moves them to the shared channel; hosted consolidation merges speaker0's two labels while keeping speaker1 apart, then shares the channel; the same layout with far-end speech present is left untouched on both paths.
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked -p listener2-core --lib --no-deps -- -D warnings`
- [ ] Record
title: Separate the people sharing the mic in in-person meetings
